QB3_H Q1 rewritten. The question asks for "a PSA and a PSSA"; the answer previously treated "PSA" as meaningless and covered only the PSSA half. It now answers both, identifying the intended counterpart as the MPA (Marine Protected Area). MPA legal basis stated correctly: UNCLOS neither defines nor mentions MPAs — Art. 194(5) is only the general obligation to protect rare or fragile ecosystems; CBD Art. 2 and Art. 8(a) supply the working definition; BBNJ Agreement Art. 1(9) gives the first treaty definition of an MPA and the mechanism for high-seas MPAs, in force 17 January 2026. PSSA is corrected away from a MARPOL framing: it is IMO Assembly resolution A.982(24) as amended by resolution MEPC.267(68), with submission guidance MEPC.1/Circ.510, and its legal force comes only from the attached Associated Protective Measure. A three-way distinction between MPA, PSSA and MARPOL Special Area is added, with Papahānaumokuākea as the example of an area that is both an MPA and a PSSA. Tag 'unclos' added.

New question QB1_K Q8 on the IACS Common Structural Rules (CSR). Scope now stated with the construction-contract applicability: the original CSR for bulk carriers (90 m and above) and double-hull oil tankers (150 m and above) apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 April 2006; the harmonised CSR BC & OT (in force 1 July 2015) apply to contracts dated on or after 1 July 2015; IACS PR No. 29 defines 'contracted for construction'. Clarified that CSR scope is not the same as SOLAS II-1 Reg. 3-10 (GBS) scope: GBS applies at 150 m and above for both ship types (Res. MSC.290(87), in force 1 Jan 2012; contract 1 Jul 2016 / keel 1 Jul 2017 / delivery 1 Jul 2020) and excludes ore carriers and combination carriers, so a 120 m bulk carrier can be a CSR ship but not a Reg. 3-10 ship. Corrected the 'why is CSR mandatory' explanation away from both 'IACS made it mandatory' and 'SOLAS makes CSR mandatory' to the four-step chain (class rules; flag/RO statutory and commercial framework; Reg. 3-10 requires conforming RO/Administration structural rules; IACS CSR verified through the IMO GBS process, MSC 96 confirming the 12 IACS Members' rules conform). IACS's statement that CSR are the only rules complying with GBS is retained but attributed to IACS, not presented as a SOLAS requirement. Added the five-tier GBS framework (MSC.287(87) / MSC.1/Circ.1394/Rev.2) and a Ship Construction File section from MSC.1/Circ.1343 (four content groups, on-board vs shore archive, update-on-major-event rule). Time-sensitive 'CSR review underway' material kept in a separate 'Current status - not exam-essential' deep-dive. Cheat sheet updated with a Q8 flip card, two confusable-pair boxes (CSR vs GBS scope; Common Structural Rules vs Continuous Synopsis Record vs CSM) and a rapid-recall row.

PSC appeal-chain correction. The Stage 3 review deadline had been stated across the bank as '120 days from the ship's release from detention' and presented as flowing from IMO Resolution A.1206(34) itself. The resolution grants only a general, one-line right of appeal (para 2.3.11) with no numeric deadline or staged mechanism; the 3-stage chain and day-count are regional MOU procedure. The 120-day figure (measured from release) is correct only for Paris MOU; IOMOU - the regime governing Indian ports - specifies 90 days from the date of detention (Detention Review Panel procedure, Section 3.13) with a 3-member review panel (Paris MOU: 4). Corrected QB4_A Q6 (deadline and panel size), QB4_E Q8 (deadline, panel size, resolution-vs-MOU attribution) and QB4_C Q11 (still citing the superseded A.1185(33) instead of A.1206(34); the action-taken code content was already correct). The three questions now cross-link (appeal chain, action codes, IOMOU/Paris MOU comparison). This supersedes the other 16 July entry, where QB4_A Q6 and QB4_E Q8 still carried the 120-day figure. Remaining mentions of A.1185(33) in these pages are intentional, explaining the superseded resolution for exam-trap awareness.
